summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism, was admitted after a fall at home due to atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He also had community-acquired pneumonia, presenting with cough, fever, and hypoxia, and was treated with intravenous antibiotics. His heart rate was controlled with IV diltiazem and initiation of digoxin, which achieved therapeutic levels. Hyperkalemia persisted despite dialysis, attributed to medications and dietary factors, and was managed with Kayexalate and dietary counseling. He improved clinically, with resolution of infection and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with 24-hour support. Key discharge instructions included continuation of digoxin with outpatient level monitoring, strict low-potassium diet, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up with primary care, endocrinology, and nephrology.
